description: Powered tool that drives a chisel or point by hammer blows alone, with no rotation, to break concrete, masonry and tile; air, petrol and electric breakers and jackhammers included.
Tool that drives nails from a strip or coil, powered by air, gas, mains or battery.
Drill driver with an extra hammer action and an ordinary chuck, for drilling masonry and concrete.
Ratcheting handle that turns interchangeable sockets; socket sets are here too.
Clock with an open frame that shows the movement, with no case around it.
Small bag with a wrist strap and its own inner compartment, unlike a wristlet wallet.
Backpack with a rigid box-shaped body and frame, padded back and reflective panels, made for a child to carry books.
Small bag-like wallet carried on a shoulder or cross-body chain, unlike a chain wallet.
Wallet fixed by a chain to a belt loop, unlike a wallet on chain.
Wallet with a wrist strap and card slots inside but no separate inner compartment, unlike a wristlet bag.
Decorative pendant that hangs on a bag; sold apart from keyrings.
Insert with pockets and dividers placed inside a bag to arrange its contents.
Hand-held umbrella that shades the carrier from the sun, with a lace, paper, silk or sun-blocking canopy not made to shed rain.
Jewelled or ornamental clip, comb or slide fixed into the hair; a plain everyday clip is in Personal Care & Beauty.
Linked metal chain worn on its own as a necklace, sold in different link patterns.
Small badge, usually enamelled metal, pinned on as ornament; an identity badge is in Documents & Personal Records.
Lace for fastening a shoe.
Removable insole for comfort, not a medical insole.
Pad that stops a heel slipping out of a shoe.
Form that holds a shoe in shape when it is not worn.
Curved tool that helps the heel slide into a shoe.
Laceless low shoe with a closed heel and covered instep that is not a moccasin, deck shoe, espadrille or clog; includes elastic-sided, quilted and sheepskin-lined slip-ons.
A sofa made of joined sections that can form a corner or L shape.
A convertible frame whose seat cushion is the mattress, folding flat into a bed; sold with or without its mattress.
A long seat for several people, with or without a back; some have storage.
A padded seat or footrest without back or arms; some have storage.
A light folding bed on a frame, used for camping or guests (called a cot in the US).
A desk whose height adjusts between sitting and standing.
A cabinet that stands in a room and keeps cigars at a set humidity.
A bound or binder album made to hold photographic prints, sold empty.
A flat or fitted sheet of woven or knitted fabric laid over the mattress or under the top cover.
A filled top cover with loose fill in stitched channels or boxes, made to go inside a removable duvet cover; fill, fill power and tog vary.
A woven, knitted or fleece cover without fill, for a bed or a sofa; comes in different sizes and weights, including weighted blankets.
A stuffed pillow made to support the head in bed; comes in different fills, firmness and orthopaedic shapes.
A shaped foam or inflatable cushion made to hold the body in a chosen position, such as wedges and ramps; the fill varies.
A removable fabric cover for a sofa, including covers made to fit one sofa model.
A removable fabric cover for a chair, including dining and event chairs and covers made to fit one chair model.
A fabric mat laid under one place setting; hard placemats are in Kitchen & Dining.
A zipped, often waterproof or anti-allergy cover fitted under the pillowcase to guard a bed pillow.
A removable fabric cover for an upholstered bed frame or headboard, including covers made to fit one model.
Flat or shallow ceiling light that sits in a suspended-ceiling grid or on the surface and gives an even spread of light. The troffer is a panel light.
Wall light made to light the face at a mirror. The lit mirror itself is not a lamp.

also_called: track or rail lighting system · rail lighting

description: Low outdoor light standing on the ground to light a path or edge. Solar or mains power is a choice within it.
Small outdoor or step light set into a surface or low base to light a step, edge or wall.
Light rigged on a truss, bar or stand to light a stage or event.
Lamp with a base and a fixed shade or head that stands on a table. Oil, gas and candle table lamps are table lamps too.
Lamp with an adjustable arm or head made for task light, standing or clamped on. A clip-on desk lamp is a desk lamp.
Small low-output lamp that plugs in or stands to give dim light overnight, including those made for babies.
Bedside lamp that brightens gradually to wake the sleeper, with or without a radio.
Hand torch from pocket size to duty size, including dive lights. Everyday-carry and tactical torches are flashlights too.
Large-head or pistol-grip hand spotlight, a different shape from the cylindrical torch.
Light worn on the head on a band or cap mount, also called a head torch. Running, ultralight and caving versions are all headlamps.
Carried lantern lit by a battery, rechargeable cell or solar panel.

also_called: mantle fuel lantern · propane lantern · liquid fuel lantern · dual fuel lantern

description: Collapsible or rigid paper-covered lantern made to be carried as a light. One made to hang as decoration is not a lamp.

also_called: general-service bulb · A-shape bulb · GLS bulb
description: Pear-shaped bulb for ordinary lamps and fittings. Filament-style and smart bulbs are standard bulbs too.

also_called: R bulb · BR bulb · PAR bulb

description: Long straight tube light source with its own cap and holder. Fluorescent, LED and halogen tubes are all tube lights.
Flexible strip of light sources sold to light a space, such as under a cabinet or in a cove.
Cord with a plug and switch or socket made for a lamp. A pendant cord set is a lamp cord set that fits a pendant.
Crystal drop or glass diffuser made to be fitted to a chandelier or other light.
Small puck or slim bar light fixed under or inside a cabinet or shelf to light a worktop or interior. A flexible strip is a strip light.
Heavy light with a wide reflector or heat-sink body, hung or fixed under a high roof to light a large floor such as a warehouse, workshop or garage.
Slim bar lamp that clips on top of a computer monitor and throws task light onto the desk without screen glare.
Large footed vessel made as an ornament, indoors or in the garden (a cremation urn is in Religious & Ceremonial Objects).
Bowl made to be looked at or to hold small decorative items (a bowl made to hold food is in Kitchen & Dining).
Self-adhesive vinyl or film motif, pattern or lettering applied to a wall, window or furniture to decorate it.
Replica sword, gun or other weapon made for display that cannot injure, decorative wushu implements included.
Bomb, grenade, mine or artillery piece made inert and kept for display.
Plain mirror on a stand made to sit on a table or dresser (a grooming mirror is in Personal Care & Beauty).
Open holder made to hold a lit candle.
Powered device made to release fragrance into a room.
Burner or electric warmer made to melt wax melts or oil.
Essential or fragrance oil sold for a diffuser or burner (an oil sold to treat a condition is in Health, Medical & Mobility).
Holder or burner made to burn incense for scenting the home (a burner for religious rites is in Religious & Ceremonial Objects).
Bound bundle of dried herbs burned to scent or cleanse a room, not made for a named rite.
Manufactured tree made to be decorated for Christmas (a real tree is in Plants & Living Cultures).
Set of dolls made to be displayed on tiers for a festival, not made for worship.
Seasonal arrangement made to stand at an entrance for a festival.
Ornamental fountain or flowing-water feature for a garden (its pump is in Garden & Grounds).
Windsock or streamer made as a garden, festive or decorative ornament (a windsock made to show wind direction or strength is in Optical & Scientific Instruments).
Neon or LED sign made to show a lit word or motif, a decorative light that spells a message included.
Lantern made to stand or hang as decoration, lit or unlit, stone garden lanterns included.
Ring of foliage, flowers or other decoration made to hang on a door or wall as a seasonal or festive ornament (an Advent wreath made for worship is in Religious & Ceremonial Objects).
Straight-sided glass jar with a lid, often footed, made to stand on display (a jar made to store food is in Kitchen & Dining).
Small bag or pouch of scented material made to scent a drawer, wardrobe or room (an odour absorber is in Cleaning & Laundry).

Reusable display calendar of fabric, wood or card with numbered doors or pockets for the days before Christmas (one sold filled with confectionery is food; an Advent wreath is in Religious & Ceremonial Objects).
Decorative or seasonal flag made to fly from a pole bracket on a house (a country or state flag is listed under its own name).
Scented wood chips, resin or powder burned on charcoal or a heater to scent a room (incense for religious rites is in Religious & Ceremonial Objects).

also_called: outdoor key box · キーボックス

description: A kit of control panel, sensors and siren sold and compared as one burglar-alarm system.
A set of cameras and a recorder sold and compared as one system.
A dead frozen animal sold as food for reptiles; live feeders are not included.
Manufactured concentrate feed for horses: pellets, cubes, coarse mix or muesli. It may be a complete feed or a top-up feed.
Seed mix, pellets, egg food, millet spray or treats made for pet cage and aviary birds. Wild-bird food is under Birds, in Wild bird food.
Viewer that boosts available light to show a scene in the dark.
Viewer that shows a scene by the heat it gives off.
Telescope that gathers light with a primary mirror and a flat secondary mirror at the side of the tube; the Dobsonian is a version of it.
Telescope with a sensor and no eyepiece that shows the sky on a screen or app.
Telescope made to observe the Sun in hydrogen-alpha light.
Microscope with its own sensor that shows the image on a screen or computer.
Loupe or magnifier on a headband or clip; also called a binocular loupe.
Glasses with a solar filter made for looking at the Sun.
Mechanical model of the Sun, planets and moons.
Instrument that models the sky for finding the positions of stars and the time.
Projector that shows the night sky on a dome or wall.
Instrument that reads the air temperature indoors or outdoors; a working Galileo thermometer counts here.
Set of instruments that measures several weather quantities together, with a display; sensor count and shielding vary by model.
Instrument that measures pollutants or particles in the air.
Freezer or ultra-low-temperature unit made for cold storage of samples; laboratory refrigerators are included.
Ventilated cabinet that draws fumes from work on samples away from the user.
Kit made to teach science through experiments, sold by subject such as chemistry, physics and electricity, biology, earth and space, or crystals and materials.
Camera made only to fit a telescope.
Camera or adapter made to fit only one kind of microscope.
Tripod made to carry a telescope mount head, sold apart from the mount; a universal photo tripod is in Cameras & Photography.
Instrument that splits light from a sample into a spectrum and measures it (UV-Vis, infrared, Raman, emission); a hand spectroscope counts here.
Small sighting device fitted on a telescope tube to aim it: finderscope, right-angle finder, red-dot or ring sight. The polar scope is listed separately.
Filter for a telescope eyepiece barrel, filter wheel or camera that passes chosen wavelengths (colour, moon, light-pollution, nebula, narrowband); solar filters are listed separately.
Objective lens that screws into a microscope nosepiece (RMS or M25 thread), sold apart from the stand; class and tube-length standard vary.
Eyepiece made for a microscope tube (23.2 or 30 mm and other barrels), sold apart from the stand; wide-field type and power vary.
